QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_25

question.text: In the SPAN margin system, the standard risk array uses 16 scenarios. If Scenario 7 uses +1/3 of the price scan range and +2/3 of the volatility scan range, what is the coverage fraction of the resulting loss in Scenario 7?

answer.text: 100% — Scenarios 1 through 14 cover their computed profit/loss at full (100%) coverage
35% — the coverage equals the fraction of the price scan range used (1/3 = 33.33%, rounded to 35%)
67% — the coverage fraction matches the volatility scan range fraction (2/3)
50% — all intermediate scenarios are covered at half their computed loss

explanation.text: The Logic: In the SPAN methodology, the standard risk array consists of 16 what-if scenarios. Scenarios 1 through 14 — including Scenario 7 with its specified fraction of the price scan range and volatility scan range — are evaluated and their computed profit/loss is taken at full (100%) coverage. The two extreme scenarios (15 and 16), representing very large up/down price moves, are typically taken at a reduced coverage fraction to balance tail-risk protection against over-margining. The Trap: Candidates often confuse the fractions of the price and volatility scan ranges used within a particular scenario (the inputs that shape the scenario) with the coverage fraction applied to its computed loss (the output weighting). These are distinct concepts; the reduced coverage applies only to the two extreme scenarios, not to Scenario 7. Note: The specific Scenario 7 inputs (+1/3 price scan range and +2/3 volatility scan range) and the 100% coverage rule for Scenarios 1-14 were not located in the cited workbook pages (Currency p.172-p.174; IRD p.253-p.255; Equity p.160-p.162), which support SPAN's 16-scenario risk-array concept in general but not the specific scenario detail. The framing above relies on general SPAN methodology rather than a workbook citation.
